findings.rationale: request_once accepts a slot while its ledger state is PLANNED, performs and parses the provider response, and returns without advancing the slot. The outer executor journals provider acceptance only afterward. This violates the required before-parsing per-native-call journal and permits direct or concurrent reuse of the same still-PLANNED slot, leaving the ledger unable to prove the actual call count.
findings.required_action: Atomically and durably claim each planned slot before provider I/O, journal native acceptance before response parsing, reject every subsequent invocation for that slot, bind the claim to the fixed ledger and failure latch, and test concurrent and direct replay.
findings.title: Provider I/O precedes an indivisible per-slot ledger transition

findings.rationale: The sealed adapter makes one HTTP request per invocation, but validation admits the same authorized PLANNED attempt repeatedly until the outer executor appends native identifiers. A direct caller can also retain a PLANNED slot after request_once returns. Consequently 24 preallocated slots do not impose an upper bound of 24 actual provider requests.
findings.required_action: Make the adapter one-shot per preallocated slot through a durable atomic pre-I/O claim and add adversarial direct, repeated, and concurrent invocation tests proving that 24 slots permit no more than 24 actual provider requests.
findings.title: The one-request adapter is replayable for an authorized slot

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Model-call and release decisions derive from fixed hashed authorization artifacts, and release remains fail-closed at R0-R2.
The importer fixes the bundle identity, replays manifest bytes and modes, validates schema and raw attempt provenance, and rejects non-identical or non-accepting review pairs.
Any revise result, open P0/P1, stage revision, or bootstrap-disposition mismatch prevents accepted receipts and authorization.
Claim and stage validation is pinned to the active candidate, complete source inventory, and parsed stage-specific artifacts.
Provider I/O and parsing occur while the attempt remains PLANNED; native acceptance is journaled only after the adapter returns, and the same slot is replayable.
The executed closure includes Runtime, build metadata, runner/helper bytes, explicit test/lint configuration, and all 192 materialized upstream tracked files.
Only the bounded T2 bootstrap path is reachable before R3; enumerated non-bootstrap completion sites require the post-R3 gate.
Full-test approval requires separate two-run AI evidence and is consumed atomically before test access; R0-R2 confers no test access.
The final preregistration coherently fixes the 216-case universe, denominators, adapter, ledger, upstream tree, and final R2 environment before any permitted result-access timestamp.
Serving gates rebuild summaries from fixed raw receipts exactly covering a reconciled attempt ledger.
Audit identity is constrained to PRIMARY AI, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh raw process evidence, and AI_INDEPENDENT_PER_USER_POLICY.
R0-R2 state uses one globally hash-chained append-only ledger, reconciled to the checkpoint and six stage bindings.
Caller-supplied review objects cannot authorize calls or release; only fixed imported artifacts and active identities are accepted.
Test approval is imported from fixed raw audit evidence and consumed at the sole test boundary.

The successor requirement for caller-selected ledgers is met: fixed ledger/latch paths, exclusive global capability, deterministic 24-slot manifest, rejection of alternatives, and a second-executor negative test. The distinct per-slot adapter replay remains under DG10-C4-AI-021.
Runtime build support including script.py.mako is materialized and included in the executed closure.
The immutable amendment and importer require xhigh; the interrupted max process has no acceptance effect.
The independently rebuilt wheel is retained, byte-hashed, and identical to the content-addressed source wheel.
The fixed approval is atomically consumed before the test callback and cannot be reused.
Collection, pytest, and Ruff use explicit project configuration, with the nested configuration included in the closure.
The adapter is one-request-per-invocation but not one-request-per-slot; a still-PLANNED slot can be replayed before outer-ledger acceptance is written.
Freeze times describe completed preregistration, result access must be strictly later, and no future-effective access assertion is used.
The R1 subordinate contract validates the complete 412-entry active internal source inventory, and ledger reconciliation checks its internal candidate and source identity.

Enumerated completion-capable clients require either fixed bootstrap authorization or the post-R3 gate. The replay defect requires an already authorized planned bootstrap slot and is therefore a bounded-call P1, not an unauthenticated direct-client P0.

DG10-R0.rationale: The R0 replay itself is semantically closed: all 201 materialized members and controls replay, historical NO-GO is immutable, the 24 unique parent findings and successor wording are complete, and candidate succession is preserved. However, the audit rule forbids an ACCEPTED stage decision while any parent P0/P1 remains open, so R0 must remain REVISE with the R1 P1 findings open.

DG10-R1.rationale: Artifact-derived authorization, AI identity, test access, release, fixed paths, and immutable ledgers are otherwise fail-closed, but actual provider I/O occurs while a slot remains replayable in PLANNED state. The implementation therefore neither proves a maximum of 24 actual provider requests nor journals native acceptance before parsing.

DG10-R2.rationale: The R2 replay itself is semantically closed: source and rebuilt wheels are byte-identical, wheel RECORD and 61 packaged Runtime modules replay, fresh frozen install/import captures are coherent, collection and pytest report 250 passing tests, Ruff passes with explicit configuration, and the 375-file execution closure plus 192-file upstream tree replay exactly. Nevertheless, ACCEPTED is prohibited while the two parent P1 findings remain open, so R2 must remain REVISE.
